who: Head pointer and eye tracking users
People who cannot hold a press
takeaways: Anything done by dragging can also be done with a single pointer and no drag: taps or clicks. New in WCAG 2.2, Level AA.
It covers sortable lists, sliders, kanban cards, resizable panels and map panning.
Keyboard support does not count here. The alternative must work with a pointer. Keyboard access is 2.1.1.
Exceptions: dragging is essential, or the drag is set by the browser and you have not changed it.
failures: Reorder handles with no move up or down option
A slider that only responds to dragging the thumb
File upload that only accepts drag and drop
check: For every draggable element, find the tap or click path that does the same job.
Try each drag task with single clicks only, never holding the button down.
Check that the alternative is visible or easy to find, not a hidden gesture.

quiz.question: A kanban board lets people drag cards between columns. The cards are also keyboard operable. What else does it need?
options: A “Drag here” hint on each column
A “Move to” menu on each card
quiz.why: Keyboard support helps keyboard users, but someone using a head pointer or a shaky hand still cannot hold and drag. A move menu gives them a click-only path.

spec: For each drag interaction, specify the single-pointer alternative: buttons, a menu, or tap to pick up and tap to place.
For sliders, state that tapping the track sets the value, or add step buttons.
Note any drag you treat as essential, and why.
review: How would someone do this without ever holding the button down?
Is the alternative findable, or only in a help article?
Is this a drag or a path-based gesture like a swipe? Swipes are 2.5.1.
tradeoff: Drag and drop feels direct and fast, and extra buttons add clutter. Keep the drag, and put the alternative in a menu on the item, so it is there when needed and quiet when not.
system: Every draggable component ships with its non-drag alternative built in, such as a “Move” menu on sortable rows and step buttons on sliders.
pitch: Dragging is one of the hardest things to do with a shaky hand or a head pointer. One menu item turns a blocked task into a finished one.
